title: One gradient, every direction
sub: The rate of change in direction v is ∇f · v. Watch it as v turns.

frames.caption: f(x, y) = x² + 3y², at the point (1.2, 0.6). The ellipses are level curves; the orange arrow is ∇f = (2.4, 3.6). Blue is a unit direction v. Its directional derivative is the dot product: D<sub>v</sub>f = ∇f · v. Due east, that is just ∂f/∂x = 2.40.
Rotating v. D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and ∇f: 3.88 here. The aqua circle traces this value in every direction where it is positive.
Pointing along the gradient: the largest possible rate, D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| = 4.33. This is why the gradient is called the direction of steepest ascent.
Rotating v. D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and ∇f: 4.32 here. The aqua circle traces this value in every direction where it is positive.
Due north, D<sub>v</sub>f is ∂f/∂y = 3.60. The partial derivatives are just two of the infinitely many directional derivatives.
Rotating v. D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and ∇f: 1.92 here. The aqua circle traces this value in every direction where it is positive.

Perpendicular to the gradient, along the level curve through the point (thick ellipse): D<sub>v</sub>f = 0. Walking along a level curve does not change f, which is exactly why the gradient is perpendicular to it.
Rotating v. D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and ∇f: -0.28 here. The aqua circle traces this value in every direction where it is positive.
Rotating v. D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and ∇f: -2.40 here. The aqua circle traces this value in every direction where it is positive.
Rotating v. D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and ∇f: -3.88 here. The aqua circle traces this value in every direction where it is positive.
Exactly opposite the gradient: the steepest descent, -4.33. Gradient descent steps this way.
Rotating v. D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and ∇f: -4.32 here. The aqua circle traces this value in every direction where it is positive.
Rotating v. D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and ∇f: -3.60 here. The aqua circle traces this value in every direction where it is positive.
Rotating v. D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and ∇f: -1.92 here. The aqua circle traces this value in every direction where it is positive.

Perpendicular to the gradient, along the level curve through the point (thick ellipse): D<sub>v</sub>f = 0. Walking along a level curve does not change f, which is exactly why the gradient is perpendicular to it.
Rotating v. D<sub>v</sub>f = |∇f| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and ∇f: 0.28 here. The aqua circle traces this value in every direction where it is positive.
